expectations.text: Flags `ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN email TEXT NOT NULL;` as high risk, explicitly because it has no default and will fail against existing rows in the table
expectations.evidence: '[high] ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN email TEXT NOT NULL ... will fail immediately ... those rows have no value for the new column'.

expectations.text: Describes `CREATE INDEX idx_users_email ON users(email);` as a lock risk that blocks writes to `users` for the duration of the build while reads keep working (a SHARE lock), and recommends `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY` as the fix — it must NOT claim the index build takes an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock
expectations.evidence: 'Takes a SHARE lock for the entire duration of the index build. Reads continue, but writes to users are blocked'; fix is CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY, named as SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE.

expectations.text: Flags the absent down/rollback migration as a reversibility gap
Gives the ordered three-step fix for the email column — add it nullable or with a default, backfill existing rows, then apply NOT NULL — rather than only naming the problem
expectations.evidence: Three numbered SQL steps: add nullable, backfill, ALTER COLUMN SET NOT NULL.

expectations.text: Does not flag `ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN nickname TEXT;` (nullable, no default) as a risk — restraint / false-positive check
expectations.evidence: FIXED: 'The two ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN statements take ACCESS EXCLUSIVE only for a catalog update (milliseconds, no table scan or rewrite), so they are not a practical lock concern.' nickname is no longer a finding.

expectations.text: Uses the skill's sectioned report structure: findings grouped under named risk categories (data-loss, lock, reversibility, backfill, index) with a severity tag per finding and a closing overall verdict, rather than one flat run of prose
expectations.evidence: Data-loss / Lock / Reversibility / Backfills / Indexes sections, severity per finding, verdict 'Blocks deployment.'
